title: Kessler Care Prepaid Maintenance Plans Sale Rules: Eligibility, Price and Term
content:
# Sale Rules — Kessler Care Prepaid Maintenance Plans

## 1. Vehicle eligibility
A plan is sold only on a vehicle that meets every one of these conditions:
- its vehicle condition is among the plan's eligible vehicle conditions;
- its age at sale (sale year minus model year) does not exceed the plan's greatest vehicle age;
- its odometer at sale does not exceed the plan's greatest odometer at sale;
- if it has a diesel engine, the plan accepts diesel-engine vehicles.

## 2. One active plan per vehicle
A vehicle carries at most the plan's maximum number of active plans (one). **A vehicle that already has an active maintenance plan cannot be sold another.** This is judged from the system's plan records for that vehicle and their status, not from the customer's account of them.

## 3. Price
(a) A plan sold on the vehicle's purchase deal is priced at the retail plan price less the bundle discount, rounded to the cent.
(b) A plan bought on its own is priced at the retail plan price and is offered only where the plan may be bought on its own.

**Status of clause 3(b).** As to price, clause 3(b) is **no longer in force** for two kinds of sale. For both, the plan is still offered only where it may be bought on its own.
- A **fleet addendum** within the scope of the fleet addendum pricing rule: a Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit plan addendum a fleet customer buys on its own for the unit delivered on its single Fleet Vehicle Purchase Agreement standing in delivered status. It takes the fleet addendum price. A retail Kessler Care plan bought on its own is not such an addendum.
- A **replacement purchase** within the scope of the retail replacement pricing rule: a Kessler Care Essentials, Plus or Premium plan bought on its own for the vehicle on the customer's single Kessler vehicle purchase deal standing in delivered status, carrying the same plan name as the replaced plan. It takes the retail plan price set by that rule. A fleet addendum is not such a purchase.

Every other retail plan bought on its own is still priced at the retail plan price. Every other fleet plan bought on its own is still priced at the retail plan price, less the fleet volume discount where the fleet volume threshold is reached.

## 4. Term
The term ends at the expiration date or at the expiration odometer, whichever comes first.
- The expiration date is the sale date plus the plan's term months, counted as calendar months. A month without that day ends on its last day.
- The expiration odometer is the odometer at sale plus the plan's term miles.

## 5. Loading
On sale, the plan's included visits are loaded to the plan.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical inputs)
- **Bundle price:** a hypothetical retail price of 760.00 with a bundle discount of 0.05 gives 760.00 less 38.00, or 722.00.
- **Expiration date:** a hypothetical sale dated 29 February of a leap year on a 24-month term expires on 28 February two years later, because that month has no 29th day. A sale dated 12 June on a 36-month term expires on 12 June three years later.
- **Expiration odometer:** a hypothetical odometer of 8,420 at sale on a 25000-mile term gives an expiration odometer of 33,420.
- **Eligibility edge:** a vehicle whose age at sale equals the plan's greatest age is eligible; one year older is not.
